benchmark.category: a daily sales input and pivot reporting app for coffee stand operators
benchmark.users: a single owner-operator entering daily omset, QRIS, cup counts and SPG shifts for about 28 stands on a phone and exporting pivot and payroll reports

requirements.source_phrase: Only me, with a password login
requirements.statement: Opening the app while signed out shows a password login screen in Bahasa Indonesia; signing in with arielaug78@gmail.com and AmkOwner2026! lands on the Input Harian tab, and a wrong password keeps the user on the login screen with a visible error and no access to any stand data.
requirements.notes: Single-owner app: no sign-up, no guest mode, no second role.

requirements.source_phrase: Only me, with a password login
requirements.statement: POST /api/auth/login returns a Bearer token for arielaug78@gmail.com with password AmkOwner2026! and refuses any other password with an error and no token; every other /api route returns 401 without a valid token and leaks no data.
requirements.notes: Credentials come from required_credentials; the build uses Bearer tokens per the agent context note.

requirements.source_phrase: Only me, with a password login
requirements.statement: Exactly one user account exists on a fresh install, arielaug78@gmail.com with password AmkOwner2026!, and it signs in without any manual seeding step.
requirements.notes: Seed values from required_credentials; later phases seed from this exact pair.

requirements.source_phrase: Bahasa Indonesia
requirements.statement: Every visible label, button, tab, status pill, empty state and error message on every screen is in Bahasa Indonesia (Input Harian, WA Generator, Pivot & Export, Pengaturan, Simpan Sekarang, Tersinkronisasi Server), with no English left in user-facing copy.
requirements.notes: The user's answer to the language question.

requirements.source_phrase: Bahasa Indonesia
requirements.statement: API responses that carry user-facing text (validation errors, save failures, auth errors) return Bahasa Indonesia messages alongside a machine-readable code, and no user-facing message is English-only.
requirements.notes: Backend half of the language requirement.

requirements.source_phrase: containing the Date Picker
requirements.statement: The sticky top header of Input Harian contains a date picker that defaults to today; choosing another date loads that date's stored values into the stand cards and the WA preview shows that date.
requirements.notes: Header is frosted glass and sticky per the design section.

requirements.source_phrase: Tersimpan di HP (Draft Lokal)
requirements.statement: The header sync pill shows the local-draft state while there are unsaved edits and switches to the synced state only after the server confirms the save; editing any field again returns it to the local-draft state.
requirements.notes: Paranoid half: a control that renders must change its own state.

requirements.source_phrase: once confirmed saved in the Laravel database
requirements.statement: POST /api/daily-input returns success only after the rows are committed and a failure status with a message when the write fails, so the client can tell synced from draft and never shows a false success.
requirements.notes: A save that fails must leave nothing half-written for that date.

requirements.source_phrase: Quick Category Filter
requirements.statement: The header offers the filter chips Semua, AMK, AMKopi and Belum Diisi; Semua shows all 28 active stands, AMK shows exactly the 18 AMK stands, AMKopi exactly the 10 AMKOPI stands, and Belum Diisi shows only stands with no saved value for the selected date.
requirements.notes: Belum Diisi semantics derived from the agent context note that dummy and real days are stored per stand.

requirements.source_phrase: render each Stand as a compact, sleek
requirements.statement: Input Harian renders each active stand as a vertical card holding a stand name badge, an Omset (Rp) numeric input, a three-column cup grid and a three-column SPG row, and TRANS has no card.
requirements.notes: TRANS excluded because is_active_input is false.

requirements.source_phrase: with live thousand-separator formatting
requirements.statement: Typing digits into a card's Omset (Rp) input shows live dot thousand separators (typing 1173000 shows 1.173.000) while the value saved and returned is the plain integer 1173000.
requirements.notes: Display formatting only; stored value must equal the digits typed.

requirements.source_phrase: 3-column grid for dynamic Cup Items
requirements.statement: Each card's middle row shows one numeric input per active cup item in sort order (default 12oz, 22oz, 16oz) and a value typed into a cup input stays attached to that stand and item after a save and reload.
requirements.notes: Grid is dynamic so items added in Settings appear here.

requirements.source_phrase: 3-column compact text inputs with autocomplete/datalist for
requirements.statement: Each parent AMK card's bottom row shows three text inputs spg1, spg2, spg3 that offer the active Master Daftar SPG names as datalist suggestions while still accepting any typed name.
requirements.notes: Amended: the managed Master Daftar SPG is now the suggestion source; the AMKOPI lock is covered separately.

requirements.source_phrase: 3-column compact text inputs with autocomplete/datalist for
requirements.statement: The API exposes the active Master Daftar SPG names so the screen can suggest them, and POST /api/daily-input stores spg1, spg2 and spg3 for that stand and date.
requirements.notes: Amended: the suggestion source is the managed master list, not only previously saved names.

requirements.source_phrase: include it in the `localStorage` draft payload `amk_draft_{YYYY-MM-DD}`
requirements.statement: Every keystroke on Input Harian writes the whole selected date's payload, including each stand's qris value, to localStorage under the key amk_draft_{YYYY-MM-DD}, replacing the previous draft for that date.
requirements.notes: Amended: qris joins the date-level draft payload.

requirements.source_phrase: automatically restore un-synced data from
requirements.statement: Refreshing, reopening or regaining connectivity on Input Harian for a date with an unsynced draft restores the draft values into the cards, and the draft is cleared once the server confirms the save.
requirements.notes: Restore must prefer the newer of local draft and server row.

requirements.source_phrase: every 1.5 seconds of inactivity
requirements.statement: After the user stops typing for about 1.5 seconds the form sends a background POST /api/daily-input for the selected date, and the sync pill moves to the synced state when it succeeds.

requirements.source_phrase: Simpan Sekarang
requirements.statement: A Simpan Sekarang button saves the current date immediately and shows a visible confirmation on success and a visible failure message in Bahasa Indonesia stating the data is still only on the phone when the request fails.
requirements.notes: Failure path must not look like success.

requirements.statement: A read endpoint for a date returns one entry per stand with the stored omset, qris, 12oz, 22oz, 16oz, spg1, spg2 and spg3 values, and returns an empty result (not an error) for a date with nothing saved.
requirements.notes: Amended: qris is part of the per-stand read; effective AMKOPI SPG is covered by amkopi-spg-parent-be.

requirements.source_phrase: POST /api/daily-input
requirements.statement: POST /api/daily-input with a date and per-stand values including qris upserts one row per stand and date, stores spg1/spg2/spg3 trimmed uppercase, so a second save replaces the numbers instead of duplicating them; the stored values are returned by the read endpoint after a reload and from a new session, and a failed write leaves no partial rows for that date.
requirements.notes: Amended: qris joins the upsert and SPG normalization is applied on the server.

requirements.source_phrase: Seed the database with these exact initial items and stands so the app works out-of-the-box without manual setup.
requirements.statement: After a fresh seed the items table holds exactly three active items - 12oz (code_wa Ck, sort_order 1), 22oz (Cb, 2) and 16oz (Csdng, 3) - and the cup inputs on every card derive from them in sort order.
requirements.notes: Exact initial master data; later phases assert these three rows.

requirements.source_phrase: 28 Active Form Input Stands
requirements.statement: After a fresh seed the stands table holds the 28 active input stands with the exact form_name, category, input_order 1-28, wa_group, wa_order, wa_name, omset_name, percup_name, show_csedang_wa and extra_wa_suffix values the user lists, plus TRANS with is_active_input false, wa_group 2, wa_order 5, wa_name TRANS and show_csedang_wa true, and no other stand, with the active-stands endpoint returning exactly those 28.
requirements.notes: The full per-stand table is the source of the WA order, the pivot rows and the AMK/AMKopi split; later phases compare field by field.

requirements.source_phrase: extra_wa_suffix
requirements.statement: The seeded overrides that differ from the stand name are stored and used: form_name TP has wa_name TP 1, omset_name TP-1 and percup_name TP; form_name AMK PREMIUM has wa_name TP 2, omset_name TP-2, percup_name AMK PREMIUM and show_csedang_wa true; R-1 carries extra_wa_suffix ', PTT 0'; WTC and KAZA have show_csedang_wa true.
requirements.notes: These overrides drive the WA text and the pivot row labels.

requirements.source_phrase: Copy ke WhatsApp
requirements.statement: The WA Generator tab shows a live preview of the report for the selected date, regenerated as soon as any saved value changes, alongside a Copy ke WhatsApp button.

Every value the WA preview renders - the stands with wa_group, wa_order, wa_name, show_csedang_wa and extra_wa_suffix, and the omset and cup values for the date - comes from the API exactly as seeded and saved, so the same date produces the same report in a new session.
requirements.notes: The build note and lib/wa.js suggest the text is assembled client-side; the server contract is that master data and daily values are returned unchanged.

requirements.source_phrase: TGL {DD/MM}
requirements.statement: The WA preview renders three blocks each headed 'TGL DD/MM' for the selected date with stands numbered from 1 inside their wa_group in wa_order - group 1 with 12 lines (WTC first, GC last), group 2 with 6 lines (R-1, R-2, SUNCITY, LIPPO, TRANS, R-4), group 3 with 11 lines (PTC then AMKopi R-1 to AMKopi BG-L2) - separated by blank lines and followed by the Keterangan footer.
requirements.notes: Line count and order follow the user's template exactly; a single misplaced line fails this check.

requirements.source_phrase: Exact WA Output Template Structure
requirements.statement: Each AMK stand line reads '{omset},Ck {12oz},Cb {22oz}' and each AMKOPI line in group 3 reads '{omset},Ck {12oz}' followed by a single trailing space, with the numbers formatted as described.
requirements.notes: Trailing space on AMKOPI lines is part of the contract and is easy to lose.

requirements.source_phrase: Format numbers with dot thousand separators
requirements.statement: Every number in the WA preview uses dot thousand separators (1173000 renders as 1.173.000) and renders 0 when the value is empty or zero, with no decimals and no currency symbol anywhere in the text.

requirements.source_phrase: print empty space after label if empty
requirements.statement: For any cup whose value is 0 or empty the label is printed with an empty space after it (for example '0,Ck ,Cb ,Csdng' or 'Ck ,Cb 112') rather than a literal 0 in the cup position.
requirements.notes: Empty-versus-zero cup rendering is the most error-prone part of the template.

requirements.source_phrase: if 16oz is 0/empty
requirements.statement: Only stands with show_csedang_wa true (WTC, KAZA, TP 2, TRANS) print a Csdng segment - ',Csdng ' with no value when 16oz is 0 or empty and ',Csdng {val}' when it is greater than zero - and no other stand prints Csdng.
requirements.notes: show_csedang_wa comes from the seeded stand rows, including TRANS.

requirements.source_phrase: 1. R-1 : {omset},Ck {12oz},Cb {22oz}, PTT 0
requirements.statement: The R-1 line ends with the seeded suffix ', PTT 0' after its Cb segment and no other line carries that suffix.
requirements.notes: Comes from extra_wa_suffix on R-1.

requirements.source_phrase: TRANS : 0,Ck ,Cb ,Csdng
requirements.statement: TRANS appears as the fifth line of group 2 reading 'TRANS : 0,Ck ,Cb ,Csdng ' with empty Ck and Cb values and a Csdng segment, even though TRANS has no card on the input form and no entered values.
requirements.notes: Inactive stand that still prints in WA group 2.

requirements.source_phrase: Total AMK : {total_omset_amk}
requirements.statement: The footer line 'Total AMK : {value}' equals the sum of Omset across all AMK stands for the selected date (groups 1 and 2 plus PTC), formatted with dot separators and 0 when everything is empty, and it never includes AMKOPI omset and never subtracts Kurma.
requirements.notes: Only addition, no multiplication and no netting of Kurma.

requirements.source_phrase: Total AMKopi : {total_omset_amkopi}, Ck {total_ck_amkopi}
requirements.statement: The footer line 'Total AMKopi : {sum of AMKOPI omset}, Ck {sum of 12oz across AMKOPI stands}' adds the AMKOPI 12oz cups separately from the AMKOPI omset sum and keeps both independent of Total AMK.
requirements.notes: Second total aggregates 12oz across the ten AMKOPI stands.

requirements.source_phrase: Total Kurma : 0, Cb 0
requirements.statement: The footer always contains the literal line 'Total Kurma : 0, Cb 0' unchanged whatever the day's data.

requirements.source_phrase: Pure mathematical addition
requirements.statement: Every figure in the WA report is a plain addition of stored values; no figure is a cup count multiplied by a price or otherwise derived by multiplication.
requirements.notes: The user calls this a strict business rule.

requirements.source_phrase: Copy ke WhatsApp
requirements.statement: Pressing Copy ke WhatsApp copies the exact preview text with its line breaks and spaces to the clipboard and shows a visible confirmation in Bahasa Indonesia.
requirements.notes: Clipboard access may need a permission grant in the test browser; the copied string is compared to the preview character by character.

requirements.source_phrase: provide 3 separate financial matrix tabs that all share the **exact same 50 fixed rows**
requirements.statement: The Pivot & Export tab offers selectable OMSET, QRIS, SISA TUNAI, PERCUP, SAL (Gaji SPG) and SPG PER STAND matrices for the chosen start and end dates; OMSET, QRIS and SISA TUNAI each render the provisional 50 rows with date columns (1) through (31).
requirements.notes: Amended: the previous three-matrix contract is superseded by the QRIS/SISA and SAL redesign.

requirements.source_phrase: provide 3 separate financial matrix tabs that all share the **exact same 50 fixed rows**
requirements.statement: For an inclusive start-end range the pivot data endpoint returns per-stand omset, per-stand qris, per-stand sisa tunai (omset minus qris), the cup sums, the SAL matrix of dates against unique SPG names with WA stand names in cells, and the per-stand SPG view with one name per cell; it includes TRANS and placeholder rows, resolves AMKOPI to its parent SPG, and returns blanks or zeros for a range with no data rather than an error.
requirements.notes: Amended: QRIS, SISA TUNAI, SAL and per-stand SPG are added to the previous Omset/Percup/SPG response.

requirements.source_phrase: appears in the Omset & Percup pivot rows
requirements.statement: The Omset and Percup matrices both contain a TRANS row carrying its summed values even though TRANS has no card on the input form.

requirements.source_phrase: percup_name
requirements.statement: Pivot rows are labelled with the seeded measure-specific names - omset_name in the Omset matrix (for example TP-1, TP-2) and percup_name in the Percup matrix (for example TP, AMK PREMIUM) - and each stand appears once per measure.

requirements.source_phrase: included as separate worksheets (`OMSET`, `QRIS`, `SISA TUNAI`) when clicking **"Download Excel (.xlsx)"**
requirements.statement: Pressing Download Excel (.xlsx) on Pivot & Export downloads one .xlsx workbook that opens with at least the sheets OMSET, QRIS, SISA TUNAI, PERCUP, SAL and SPG PER STAND, each holding the rows and values its screen mode shows.
requirements.notes: Amended: the earlier exactly-three-sheet contract is replaced by the six-sheet export.

requirements.source_phrase: Dynamic Master Data for Stands & Items
requirements.statement: The Settings tab lists every stand and every item and lets the owner add, edit, reorder or deactivate them, and a saved change is visible on Input Harian, in the WA preview and in the pivot after the next load.

requirements.source_phrase: Dynamic Master Data for Stands & Items
requirements.statement: Create and update calls on the stands and items resources persist every field the Settings form sends, the read endpoints return them after a reload and from a new session, and a deactivated stand drops out of the active input list while its historical saved values remain readable.

requirements.source_phrase: berikan data dummy
requirements.statement: The Settings screen has a button that generates dummy daily data so the app has data out of the box, and the generated days appear in Input Harian, the WA preview and the pivot.
requirements.notes: The user asked for dummy data; the seven-day span and the is_dummy flag come from the agent context note.

requirements.source_phrase: berikan data dummy
requirements.statement: The generate-dummy action creates daily rows flagged is_dummy for the seven days ending today, with values for the stands and items, and running it again does not corrupt or duplicate real owner-saved rows.
requirements.notes: Seven days and is_dummy=true are build-described values, recorded here so later phases can seed and clean up deterministically.

requirements.source_phrase: berikan tombol untuk clear all data dummy nya
requirements.statement: The Settings screen has a Hapus Semua Dummy button that asks for confirmation and, once confirmed, removes only the dummy rows while days the owner saved himself still show their values afterwards.

requirements.source_phrase: berikan tombol untuk clear all data dummy nya
requirements.statement: Clearing dummy data deletes exactly the rows flagged is_dummy and no others in one operation; real owner-saved rows counted before and after are unchanged and still readable.
requirements.notes: Destructive action: the paranoid form checks that it cannot reach real rows.

requirements.statement: The API marks each stand as filled or unfilled for a date from the stored rows, so the Belum Diisi chip shows exactly the stands with no saved value for that date and shows an explicit empty message when every stand is filled.
requirements.notes: Assumption recorded: a stand counts as filled once it has a saved row for the date, whatever the values; a stand with an all-zero row counts as filled.

requirements.statement: Typing letters or a minus sign into an omset or cup input leaves the field numeric and no non-numeric or negative value is ever saved or included in a total.
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of the numeric-input requirement.

requirements.statement: When the autosave request fails (offline or server error) the pill stays on the local-draft state and a visible message says the data is not yet on the server; no success state is shown and nothing typed is lost.
requirements.notes: Failure path of an action that otherwise succeeds.

requirements.statement: With the network disabled, values typed into a date survive a page reload from the local draft, and on reconnect they sync and read back from the server for that same date.
requirements.notes: Offline-resilience half of the localStorage feature.

requirements.statement: A date with nothing saved renders every card with empty omset and cup fields, the WA preview built from it prints 0 and empty cup labels without crashing, and the pivot for that single day shows zeros.
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of 'a list is shown': the zero-row case.

requirements.statement: Choosing an earlier date is accepted, shows that day's saved values and saves edits to that day, because daily sales entries are history rather than a future booking.
requirements.notes: Date-rule paranoid form: past dates are legitimate for a ledger; the app must not refuse or silently rewrite them.

requirements.statement: Deactivating a stand in Settings removes its card from Input Harian and its line from the WA preview after reload, and reactivating it restores both without losing the values previously saved for it.
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of the master-data CRUD requirement.

requirements.statement: Exporting a range with no saved data still downloads a valid workbook containing the OMSET, QRIS, SISA TUNAI, PERCUP, SAL and SPG PER STAND sheets with their header rows rather than failing silently or producing a corrupt file.
requirements.notes: Amended for the expanded sheet list.

requirements.statement: Two saves arriving together for the same stand and date leave exactly one stored row holding the later submitted values, and no duplicate row is counted in any pivot.
requirements.notes: Uniqueness enforced by the store, not only by the screen.

requirements.statement: Each pivot cell equals the sum of the stored daily values for that stand and measure across the inclusive range, and changing one day's value by X changes that cell by exactly X.
requirements.notes: Calculation class: aggregates equal the sum of their parts in Rupiah and whole cups.

requirements.statement: A pivot range whose start equals its end reports exactly that single day's values, and a range always includes both its start and end dates and no day outside them.
requirements.notes: Boundary case of the date-range rule.

requirements.statement: For the same date a stand's omset shows the same number on the input card, in the WA report, in the pivot Omset matrix and in the exported sheet, in Rupiah with dot separators in the text contexts and as a plain number in the sheet.
requirements.notes: A value changed in one place must change everywhere it is shown.

requirements.source_phrase: Strictly Apple Monochrome
requirements.statement: Every screen uses only the Apple monochrome palette (black #000000, off-black #1D1D1F, white #FFFFFF, gray #F5F5F7, border gray #D2D2D7) with solid black primary buttons and white text, 1px gray borders, and no colourful accent anywhere.
requirements.notes: Visual class; the shell serves the stylesheet the theme lives in.

requirements.source_phrase: never scrolls horizontally
requirements.statement: At a 390px-wide viewport the Input Harian page has no horizontal scrollbar, every stand card fits inside the viewport, and the header controls and the four-tab bottom bar stay fully visible while the list scrolls.
requirements.notes: Mobile-first layout class; also checked at a desktop width for overlap and clipping.

requirements.source_phrase: tabular-nums
requirements.statement: All numeric inputs and financial outputs use tabular numerals and the system sans-serif stack (SF Pro Display, Inter, -apple-system), so digits align in columns and no numeric field uses a proportional figure font.
requirements.notes: Visual class; typography is part of the design system.

requirements.source_phrase: Sticky bottom frosted-glass navigation bar with 4 tabs
requirements.statement: The sticky bottom bar has exactly four tabs - Input Harian, WA Generator, Pivot & Export, Settings - each opens its screen without a full page reload, the active tab is visibly distinct from the others, and a browser reload returns the user to the tab they were on.
requirements.notes: UI-state class: selection survives reload and state looks different.

requirements.statement: Loading, disabled, selected and error states of the save button, the sync pill and the tabs look different from each other, and a screen whose data request fails shows an error message in Bahasa Indonesia instead of a blank page.
requirements.notes: UI-state class.

requirements.statement: Selecting a pivot range with no data shows an explicit empty or zero state inside each matrix instead of a blank panel, and the export control stays usable.
requirements.notes: UI-state class: zero-row case of a table.

requirements.statement: A sign-out control ends the session: the app returns to the login screen, discards the stored token, and sends no further authenticated requests, and the browser back button does not reveal stand, pivot or WA data.
requirements.notes: Auth class: the unstated inverse of the login requirement.

requirements.statement: After sign-out a data request made without a token is refused with 401 and returns no rows, and the sign-out call itself completes without leaving the session usable.
requirements.notes: Auth class.

requirements.statement: Opening a data screen by direct URL while signed out shows the login screen and renders no stand card, pivot value or WA text, and after signing in the user reaches the requested screen.
requirements.notes: Auth class: private data refused on a direct link.

requirements.statement: No screen offers sign-up, guest entry or password-less access, so a second person cannot create an account or reach the data without the owner password.
requirements.notes: Auth class: the user asked for 'only me'.

requirements.statement: No account-creation endpoint exists or every attempt to create a user without an authenticated owner session is refused, and every data endpoint requires a valid token.
requirements.notes: Auth class: enforced on the server, not merely hidden in the screen.

requirements.statement: A signed-in owner who reloads or reopens the app stays signed in until sign-out or token expiry, and an expired or invalid token returns them to the login screen with a message rather than an empty form.
requirements.notes: Auth class: session survives refresh and ends visibly.

requirements.statement: No password, server secret or another client's token appears in any page source, API response body or log line, and the login response carries only the token and user fields the client needs.
requirements.notes: Auth class: secrets never appear in a response or a page.

requirements.statement: Every field the input form sends for a stand and date - omset, qris, 12oz, 22oz, 16oz, spg1, spg2 and spg3 - is stored and returned unchanged by the read endpoint after a reload and from a new session, with SPG values stored trimmed and uppercase and no submitted field silently dropped.
requirements.notes: Amended: qris is added and SPG normalization is observable on read-back.

requirements.statement: The downloaded workbook's OMSET, QRIS, SISA TUNAI, PERCUP, SAL and SPG PER STAND sheets hold the same rows, columns and values the screen shows for the selected range, with SISA TUNAI equal to OMSET minus QRIS per stand per date, WA stand names in SAL cells, and numeric cells stored as numbers.
requirements.notes: Amended for the expanded export; worded by file content.

requirements.statement: The exported file's name identifies the app and the exported range (for example amk-pivot_2026-01-01_2026-01-07.xlsx) and carries the .xlsx extension that makes it open as a spreadsheet.
requirements.notes: File class: the file name says what it is.

requirements.statement: Typing a multi-digit omset produces one save request about 1.5 seconds after the last keystroke rather than one per keystroke, and a full day of entry on all 28 cards stays a small bounded number of requests.
requirements.notes: Performance class: debounce actually debounces.

requirements.statement: Input Harian renders all 28 cards and accepts typing without visible lag at phone width, and a 7-day pivot loads in about the time a single-day pivot takes over the same stands.
requirements.notes: Performance class.

requirements.statement: Leaving a tab cancels its pending autosave timer and any polling, so returning to it fires no duplicate save for a previously selected date and only one save per edit reaches the server.
requirements.notes: Performance class: no timer or subscription leaks across tab switches.

requirements.statement: Each of the four tabs and the login screen opens and renders its content with no blank page, unhandled exception or console error, including when opened by a deep link and after a hard reload.
requirements.notes: Build/deployment class.

requirements.statement: Requesting the app root and any client route (for example /pivot or /settings) returns the application shell with HTTP 200 and its JavaScript and CSS assets resolve without a 404, so a deep link or reload renders the screen instead of a server error page.
requirements.notes: Build/deployment class; also the shell that serves the stylesheet the theme lives in.

requirements.source_phrase: Laravel 11, SQLite/MySQL, Tailwind CSS, Alpine.js, and SheetJS (xlsx)
requirements.statement: The application is built on the stated stack - Laravel 11 with SQLite/MySQL, Tailwind CSS, Alpine.js and SheetJS for the spreadsheet export - and every screen works against that stack with no host hard-coded in the code.
requirements.notes: Explicit user stack. The build description names a React frontend with a Python server (files_of_reference: /app/backend/server.py, /app/frontend/src/App.js); Phase 4 must report the divergence rather than assume the stack was followed.

requirements.source_phrase: php 8.5
requirements.statement: The application runs on PHP 8.5 with no deprecation or runtime error caused by the PHP version on any screen or endpoint.
requirements.notes: Explicit user requirement; the build description suggests a non-PHP runtime, so Phase 4 reports what actually runs.

requirements.statement: Opening Input Harian selects today's date and shows the values already saved for today, so the daily entry starts on the current day without extra taps.
requirements.notes: benchmark: daily sales input apps open on today with today's figures loaded.

requirements.statement: Each stand card shows whether that stand is already filled for the selected date, and the count behind the Belum Diisi chip equals the number of cards without a saved value.
requirements.notes: benchmark: with dozens of stands the operator needs to see what is still missing before copying the report.

requirements.statement: From the date picker the owner can move to an earlier day and back to today in at most two actions, and the cards, the WA preview and the entered values follow the chosen date.
requirements.notes: benchmark: day-to-day navigation is the core repeated action of a daily entry app.

requirements.statement: A text search over the stand list narrows the cards to stands whose name matches, clearing it restores the full list for the active chip, and a search with no match shows an explicit empty message.
requirements.notes: benchmark: 28 stands make a name search a table-stake control.

requirements.statement: Input Harian shows the running total omset for the selected date so the owner can sanity-check the figure before copying the WhatsApp report, and it equals the sum of the day's omset values across the active stands.
requirements.notes: benchmark: daily entry apps show a running daily total that matches the report.

requirements.statement: Leaving or closing the page while a draft is still unsynced triggers a visible warning or the browser's unsaved-changes prompt, and the draft is still recoverable afterwards.
requirements.notes: benchmark: data-entry apps warn before dropping unsaved work.

requirements.statement: Adding a cup item in Settings adds a matching input to every stand card, a matching column to the Percup matrix and a matching column to the exported sheet after the next load.
requirements.notes: Archetype: master data is only worth having if the dynamic form, pivot and export all follow it.

requirements.statement: Adding a stand in Settings with an input_order, wa_group, wa_order and category adds its card in that position, its line at the right number inside the right WA group, and its pivot row after reload.
requirements.notes: Archetype: the stand master data drives the form, the WA report and the pivot together.

requirements.statement: A start date later than the end date is refused with a visible message in Bahasa Indonesia and the previously rendered matrices stay on screen rather than showing an empty or broken grid.
requirements.notes: Product shell: date-range controls validate their own order.

requirements.source_phrase: Input field: **QRIS (Rp)** (`inputmode="numeric"` with thousand-separator formatting).
requirements.statement: On each active stand card in Input Harian a QRIS (Rp) input sits after the cup and SPG fields, accepts digits with live dot thousand separators (typing 250000 shows 250.000), and the saved value is the plain integer 250000.
requirements.notes: QRIS default 0; the field is per stand and date.

requirements.source_phrase: Add a `qris` (bigInteger, default 0) column to the daily sales input table (and include it in the `localStorage` draft payload `amk_draft_{YYYY-MM-DD}`).
requirements.statement: POST /api/daily-input accepts a qris value per stand and date (default 0 when omitted), stores it as a whole-Rupiah integer, and the date read endpoint returns the same qris value after a reload and from a new session.

requirements.source_phrase: Live calculated read-only display: **Sisa Tunai (Rp)** = `Omset - QRIS` (formatted with thousand separators).
requirements.statement: On each stand card the read-only Sisa Tunai (Rp) display updates as the user types and always equals that card's Omset minus its QRIS, formatted with dot thousand separators and showing the arithmetic difference rather than a stale or clamped value.
requirements.notes: The displayed value must match the two fields above it after a reload.

requirements.source_phrase: At the sticky summary bar / bottom of the Daily Input page, display 3 live daily totals:
requirements.statement: The sticky summary bar at the bottom of Input Harian shows three live daily totals for the selected date - Total Omset Harian, Total QRIS Harian and Total Sisa Tunai Harian - where the sisa total equals Total Omset Harian minus Total QRIS Harian, all formatted with dot separators and 0 when empty.

requirements.source_phrase: **Total Omset Harian**
requirements.statement: The daily summary endpoint returns for a date the sum of stored omset across the active stands, the sum of stored qris, and their difference as total sisa tunai, computed from the stored per-stand rows and matching the values shown on the cards.
requirements.notes: Totals equal the sum of their parts and use the same stored rows the cards read.

requirements.source_phrase: Do NOT show QRIS or Sisa Tunai in the **WA Generator**.
requirements.statement: The WA Generator preview and copied text contain only gross omset and cup values and never include QRIS, Sisa Tunai or any total derived from them; adding or changing QRIS for a date leaves the WA text byte-for-byte unchanged.
requirements.notes: Strict isolation: the WhatsApp report must remain 100% unchanged.

requirements.source_phrase: hide or lock (`read-only` badge showing "SPG Mengikuti Stand Utama") the `spg1`, `spg2`, `spg3` inputs on `AMKOPI` cards
requirements.statement: On Input Harian every AMKOPI card hides or locks its spg1/spg2/spg3 inputs and shows a read-only badge 'SPG Mengikuti Stand Utama' with the parent AMK stand's current SPG names, so the owner can only type SPG names on the parent AMK card.

requirements.source_phrase: For all `AMKOPI` stands, the SPG names follow their parent `AMK` stand
requirements.statement: The API stores the parent links AMKopi R-1 -> R-1, AMKopi R-2 -> R-2, AMKopi R-4 -> R-4, AMKopi TP-1 -> TP, AMKopi TP-2 -> AMK PREMIUM, AMKopi TP-3 -> TP-3, AMKopi GC -> gc, AMKopi Delta -> delta, AMKopi BG-LL -> BG-LL and AMKopi BG-L2 -> BG-L2, and returns for each AMKOPI stand the effective SPG names inherited from that parent for the selected date without requiring separate AMKOPI SPG rows.
requirements.notes: Parent mapping from the user's list; AMKOPI must not double-enter or double-count the same SPG.

requirements.source_phrase: Normalize all SPG name inputs automatically to **UPPERCASE and trimmed**
requirements.statement: Typing an SPG name into any parent AMK card's spg1/spg2/spg3 input displays it in uppercase as the user types (typing ' mega ' shows 'MEGA') and the suggestion list matches case-insensitively.
requirements.notes: Client half of the normalization.

requirements.source_phrase: Normalize all SPG name inputs automatically to **UPPERCASE and trimmed**
requirements.statement: POST /api/daily-input trims surrounding spaces and uppercases every spg1/spg2/spg3 value before storing it, so ' mega ' is stored and returned as 'MEGA' and the same person never appears in two SAL columns because of case or spaces.

requirements.source_phrase: provide 3 separate financial matrix tabs that all share the **exact same 50 fixed rows**
requirements.statement: The Pivot & Export tab offers OMSET, QRIS and SISA TUNAI modes that each render the same provisional 50 rows with date columns (1) through (31) for the selected range, in the same row order on all three modes.
requirements.notes: The 50-row list runs from R-1 to AMKopi PTC and includes placeholder rows such as R-5, CITO, trans, GREEN TEA and THAI TEA.

requirements.source_phrase: provide 3 separate financial matrix tabs that all share the **exact same 50 fixed rows**
requirements.statement: The pivot data endpoint returns, for the selected range and each of the provisional 50 rows, the per-date omset, qris and sisa tunai (omset minus qris) values in one shared row order, with the same 50 rows for all three financial matrices.

requirements.source_phrase: **Tab/Sheet 3: `SISA TUNAI`** (Automatically calculates and displays `omset - qris` per stand per date).
requirements.statement: In the SISA TUNAI matrix and sheet every per-date cell for a stand equals that stand's stored omset minus its stored qris for the same date, and a range cell equals the sum of those daily differences; no cell is copied from the OMSET sheet or clamped at zero.

requirements.source_phrase: Each tab must have its own **"Copy untuk Google Sheets (TSV)"** button
requirements.statement: Each of the OMSET, QRIS and SISA TUNAI matrices has its own 'Copy untuk Google Sheets (TSV)' button that copies the visible matrix - row labels, date headers 1-31 and cell values - as tab-separated text and shows a visible confirmation.

requirements.source_phrase: **Columns (Horizontal Header across the top)**: Every unique SPG Name gets their own dedicated column
requirements.statement: The SAL / GAJI pivot view lists every unique SPG name as its own column and the sequential dates of the selected range down the left side, with exactly one stand name per cell and no cell containing a comma-combined pair.
requirements.notes: User also removed comma-combined SPG cells: 'Remove any comma-combined SPG cells'.

requirements.source_phrase: Nama seperti di laporan WA
requirements.statement: For each date a SPG worked, the SAL cell shows that stand's WA report name (for example 'TP 1' for form_name TP, 'AMK PREMIUM' for AMK PREMIUM) rather than the short form_name or omset_name.
requirements.notes: User answer to 'Kode stand apa yang tampil di sel Tabel Gaji SPG?'.

requirements.source_phrase: For all `AMKOPI` stands, the SPG names follow their parent `AMK` stand
requirements.statement: The SAL data endpoint returns, for the selected range, the ordered unique active SPG names as columns, one row per date, and for each SPG-date the stand's WA name resolved from the parent AMK stand (AMKOPI inherits), with no comma-joined values and AMKOPI never creating a separate SPG column entry from its parent.

requirements.source_phrase: Row `TOTAL HADIR (SHIFT)`: Automatically counts total working days/shifts for each SPG column across the selected date range for easy payroll calculation.
requirements.statement: The SAL view ends with a TOTAL HADIR (SHIFT) row that counts, for each SPG column, the number of distinct dates in the selected range on which that SPG has a stand, and the same count appears in the exported SAL sheet.

requirements.source_phrase: satu SPG tidak akan jaga dalam satu hari yang sama
requirements.statement: The SAL endpoint computes TOTAL HADIR per SPG as the count of distinct dates with a stand assignment, counting a SPG at most once per date even if the same name is entered on two stands that day, and the count equals the filled cells for that column.
requirements.notes: The user states this situation will not occur; the paranoid form prevents a double shift count if it does.

requirements.source_phrase: **Secondary View (Toggle) — Detail SPG per Stand (Separate Columns, No Commas)**
requirements.statement: A Tampilan Per Stand toggle on the SPG pivot shows one row per stand with three separate SPG 1, SPG 2 and SPG 3 cells (or three sub-columns) so each cell contains exactly one name, and AMKOPI rows show the parent AMK stand's SPG names.

requirements.source_phrase: render 3 separate sub-columns or 3 distinct rows per Stand (`SPG 1`, `SPG 2`, `SPG 3`) so every cell contains strictly **1 SPG name**
requirements.statement: The per-stand SPG endpoint returns one row per stand for the range with spg1, spg2 and spg3 as separate single-name fields, AMKOPI rows resolved to the parent SPG, and never a comma-joined string.

requirements.source_phrase: In the **Settings** tab, add a **Master Daftar SPG** section where the user can manage the list of active SPG names
requirements.statement: The Settings tab has a Master Daftar SPG section that lists the active SPG names and lets the owner add, rename and delete a name; a new name is shown uppercase and a duplicate save is refused with a visible message and no duplicate row.
requirements.notes: Duplicate refusal is the paranoid half of creating a record; the duplicate check must be case-insensitive after uppercase normalization.

requirements.source_phrase: (used for instant 1-tap autocomplete suggestions on the Daily Input form and for ordering the columns in the `SAL / SPG` payroll export).
requirements.statement: CRUD endpoints for the SPG master list persist each active name uppercased and trimmed, refuse a second name equal case-insensitively with a 409 and no new row, and the stored list drives the autocomplete suggestions and the SAL column order.

requirements.source_phrase: Pakai daftar sementara yang bisa diedit
requirements.statement: The Pivot & Export screen uses a provisional 50-row list shared by OMSET, QRIS and SISA TUNAI that starts at R-1 and ends at AMKopi PTC, includes placeholder rows such as R-5, CITO, trans, GREEN TEA and THAI TEA, and the owner can add, edit or delete rows in Settings with the change appearing in all three matrices and in the exported sheets after reload.
requirements.notes: The original omset.pdf was never provided; the build seeds a provisional editable list.

requirements.source_phrase: Pakai daftar sementara yang bisa diedit
requirements.statement: The pivot row master stores the provisional 50-row list in order, persists add, edit and delete changes, and the pivot and export endpoints return exactly those rows in that order for every financial matrix.

In Settings an AMKOPI stand's edit form has a parent-stand selector that lists the AMK stands, saves the chosen parent, and the AMKOPI card on Input Harian immediately shows the parent's SPG after reload.
requirements.notes: Build description lists stand-parent-select; needed because AMKOPI cards must resolve a parent SPG.

requirements.statement: The stand resource stores a parent_stand_id for AMKOPI stands, accepts the parent on create and update, refuses a parent that is itself AMKOPI or missing, and returns the parent id with the stand after reload.
requirements.notes: Build description: stand parent select for AMKOPI.

requirements.statement: Each OMSET, QRIS and SISA TUNAI matrix shows a TOTAL column and a TOTAL row whose cells equal the sum of the corresponding cells, with SISA TUNAI totals equal to OMSET totals minus QRIS totals.
requirements.notes: Build description lists a TOTAL row/column; benchmark: pivot sheets users reconcile against carry totals.

requirements.statement: Placeholder rows in the 50-row list that have no stand or no saved data render blank cells (not zero, not an error) in OMSET, QRIS, SISA TUNAI, the TSV copy and the exported sheets, while their row label still appears.
requirements.notes: Build description: placeholder rows blank; the user names the placeholder rows but not their blank rendering.

requirements.statement: The generate-dummy action writes a qris value for every dummy stand-day row, with at least some non-zero values across the seven days, and Hapus Semua Dummy removes exactly those rows.
requirements.notes: Build description says seven days of dummy data exist with qris; seed data should exercise the new QRIS field.
